title: Local normalization defect and its canonical completion comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X$ a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pure-dimension], $x$ a closed point, and $
u:X^
u	o X$ its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$, and $M=B/A$, with the natural inclusion and direct image on opens. The morphism $
u$ is finite and surjective; its fibre at $x$ is a finite nonempty set of closed points, and $k	o\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism for every point $y$ in that fibre. The ring $A$ is a reduced Noetherian local $k$-algebra of Krull dimension one, essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], with residue field $k$ via its structural map. Let $Q(A)$ be the localization at all elements $s$ for which $sa=0$ implies $a=0$. Then $B$ is a finite $A$-module and is the integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The module $M$ has finite length (a finite filtration with simple successive quotients), is finite-dimensional over $k$, and its length over $A$ equals $\dim_k M$. Put $H=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m_A^n$ and $C=\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak m_A^nB$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The ring $H$ is reduced Noetherian complete local of dimension one with structural residue field $k$; the canonical maps identify $C=B\otimes_A H$ with its integral closure in $Q(H)$ and induce a $k$-linear isomorphism $M\cong C/H$. If $X$ is smooth over $k$ at $x$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then $B=A$ and $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), (1)--(9), and Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion); structural residue fields over algebraically closed k. Agent specialization including the simple-filtration comparison of length with k-dimension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure] to the reduced finite-type scheme $X$. It gives finiteness and surjectivity of $\nu$, the structural injection $A\hookrightarrow B$, and identifies $B$ with the finite integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$. In particular these identifications use the actual direct-image stalk and respect localization. By [def-weil-pure-dimension], the hypothesis on $X$ says exactly that every irreducible component has dimension one. Thus [lem-trf-curve-normalization-coherent-support] applies: at the closed point $x$, $A$ is reduced Noetherian local of dimension one, essentially of finite type over $k$, and $k\to\kappa(x)$ is the structural isomorphism. It also supplies the coherent quotient sheaf $Q$ with $Q_x=B/A$ and finite closed support.

By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], the fibre of $
u$ over $x$ is finite; it is nonempty by surjectivity. To check closedness of its individual points, choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$ and use the finite integral-closure model $
u^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}T$ from [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure]. A prime $\mathfrak q$ over the maximal ideal of $x$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], since $T$ is integral over $R$. Hence each point is closed within the fibre. The fibre is a closed subset of $X^
u$ because $x$ is closed, so its points are closed in $X^
u$. In the stalk model they correspond to the primes of $B$ over $\mathfrak m_A$. Each residue field is a quotient of the finite-dimensional $k$-algebra $B/\mathfrak m_AB$, whose spanning set is given by the images of a finite $A$-generating set of $B$. Thus $\kappa(y)/k$ is finite-dimensional, and [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial] says that the structural map $k	o\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), (1), and lemma-normalize-noetherian-dim-1; algebra.tex Tags 00GS (lemma-integral-over-field), 09GR in fields.tex (lemma-algebraically-closed).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-finite-support-skyscrapers] to the coherent quotient $Q$ from step 1. The scheme is Noetherian by [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure], hence locally Noetherian as required. If $Q_x\ne0$, this lemma gives a finite filtration of $M=Q_x$ with simple successive quotients. If $Q_x=0$, the empty filtration does so. This proves finite length in all cases.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), (4), using coherent finite closed support; algebra.tex lemma-support-point.

proof.text: For each simple factor $L$ of this filtration, choose $0\ne v\in L$. Simplicity makes $A\to L$, $a\mapsto av$, surjective; its kernel is maximal since the quotient has no proper nonzero ideals. As $A$ is local, the kernel is $\mathfrak m_A$. Consequently $L\cong A/\mathfrak m_A\cong k$ via the structural map, so it has $k$-dimension one and $A$-length one. Inductively lift a $k$-basis from each quotient and append it to a basis of the preceding submodule: spanning follows by subtracting a lift, and independence follows by projecting a relation. Therefore a filtration with $r$ factors gives $\dim_k M=r$, including $r=0$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to its successive short exact sequences gives $\operatorname{length}_A M=r$ as well.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive); elementary cyclic description of simple modules over a local ring and basis lifting.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-curve-normalization-completion] to the reduced one-dimensional local $k$-algebra $A$ obtained in step 1, with its integral closure $B$. It states that $H=\widehat A$ is reduced of dimension one and canonically identifies $B\otimes_AH$ with the integral closure of $H$ in $Q(H)$. All its hypotheses, including essentially finite type, were supplied in step 1; no assertion for arbitrary reduced local rings is being used.

The Noetherian conclusion for $H$ is [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $H$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_AH$ and its residue field is canonically $A/\mathfrak m_A$. The latter is structurally $k$ by step 1, so their composite is the required structural residue-field identification. Since $A$ is Noetherian its maximal ideal is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with the module $A$ and ideal $\mathfrak m_A$: $H$ is complete for the powers $\mathfrak m_A^nH=(\mathfrak m_AH)^n$. Hence it is complete as a local ring.

Use [lem-trf-finite-colength-completion-comparison] for the injective finite ring map $A\hookrightarrow B$ and the finite filtration of $M$ from step 3. It identifies $C=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m_A^nB$ canonically with $B\otimes_AH$, respecting the structural inclusion of $H$, and gives the isomorphism $M\to C/H$ explicitly by $b+A\mapsto\iota_B(b)+H$. Combining this tensor identification with step 5 identifies this very $C$ with the integral closure of $H$ in $Q(H)$. The quotient map is $A$-linear by the cited statement; restricting scalars along $k\to A$ makes it $k$-linear. This proves the asserted canonical comparison, rather than merely an equality of dimensions.

Finally [lem-trf-curve-normalization-coherent-support] identifies the locus $N$ of normal local rings with the smooth locus and says $Q_x=0$ exactly on $N$. If $X$ is smooth at $x$, therefore $M=Q_x=B/A=0$. The structural inclusion $A\hookrightarrow B$ then has zero quotient, so it is surjective as well as injective: under the stipulated inclusion $B=A$.
